# Diver docs stale: dive described as x-locked but implemented as diagonal (AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA)

## Problem statement

The Diver (E2) documentation still describes the dive as a **vertical drop with
x locked at the formation slot**, but the implemented and shipped behaviour
(AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX) is a **diagonal parabolic dive** toward the player
position snapshotted at dive start. The resulting docs contradict the code and
can mislead future implementation, tuning, and parity work.

## Users

- **Player / observer** — reads (or is described) the Diver as a predictable
  vertical threat; the real dive is diagonal toward the snapshotted player
  position, so the stated behaviour is wrong.
- **Developer / maintainer** — relies on `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  as the authoritative guide for enemy behaviour and gym/game parity; stale
  "x locked" wording risks re-introducing a vertical-only dive or mis-scoping
  related fixes.
- **Producer / reviewer** — needs the GDD and the implementation guide to agree
  on the dive contract so acceptance criteria for Diver work are unambiguous.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want the Diver documentation to describe the actual
  diagonal dive so that I do not implement or test against a vertical-only
  trajectory.
- As a **player-facing designer**, I want the GDD to state that a mid-dive aim
  change does not alter the in-flight arc, so the Diver's dodge window is
  understood correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Stale x-locked descriptions corrected:** The three known locations
  describe the dive as diagonal (both x and y follow the quadratic bezier from
  the formation slot to the player position snapshotted at dive start) and no
  longer state that x is locked:
  - `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1 catalog row (E2, "Vertical dive
    toward player (x locked at formation slot)").
  - `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §7.3 (live aim tracking, "Dives are
    x-locked at the formation slot.").
  - `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.1 (E2 Diver, "Dives straight down toward
    the player (x locked at its formation slot — a vertical trajectory)").
- [ ] **AC2 — Snapshot semantics documented:** The docs state that the dive
  target is snapshotted at dive start, so a mid-dive aim change does not alter
  the in-flight arc (§7.3 already carries this; it must remain consistent and be
  reflected in the corrected dive description).
- [ ] **AC3 — No stale vertical-only/x-locked Diver statements remain:** A
  repository search of `docs/` for the Diver dive finds no remaining
  x-locked / vertical-only trajectory claims for E2; the correction is
  cross-referenced to the superseding work item AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX.
- [ ] **AC4 — All related documentation is updated:** The three locations above
  are updated consistently (including the GDD and the implementation guide), and
  any relevant code comments remain accurate — including the stale comment at
  `src/entities/Diver.test.ts:128-130` ("x is locked at the dive-start slot"),
  which the producer confirmed (OPEN QUESTION 1, answer (a)) is in scope as a
  **comment-only** edit (no assertion or behavioural change).
- [ ] **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Docs-only change** — no production code or runtime behaviour change; no test
  changes are expected. AC5 is a guard against accidental regressions. Exception
  (producer-confirmed, OPEN QUESTION 1 answer (a)): a **comment-only** edit to
  `src/entities/Diver.test.ts:128-130` is in scope under AC4 — no assertion or
  behavioural change.
- **Preserve existing documented semantics** — the formation-hold-while-away
  behaviour (`DIVING`/`PAUSING`/`RETURNING`, §7.6) and the "snapshot at dive
  start" seam decision are correct and must not be altered.
- **Keep GDD and implementation guide consistent** — both documents must describe
  the same dive contract; do not diverge or restate one as authoritative over the
  other without a reference.
- **Do not touch `CHANGELOG.md`** — it is managed by the ship skill's release
  pipeline.
- **No scope creep** — do not rewrite unrelated enemy documentation; record any
  additional discovered drift as a linked work item rather than folding it in.

## Existing state

- **Implemented behaviour (shipped, AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX):** `_startDive()` snapshots
  `this.target.x/y` into `_diveTargetX/Y`, computes `apexX=(startX+targetX)/2` and
  `apexY=GAME_HEIGHT*0.30`, and `_handleDive()` positions the Diver with
  `computeDivePoint(...)` — a quadratic bezier
  `P(t)=(1-t)²P0+2(1-t)tP1+t²P2` applied to **both** axes. The former x-lock
  (`setPosition(_diveStartX, point.y)`) has been removed. `setAimTarget()` documents
  the dive-start snapshot.
- **Stale docs (to be corrected):**
  - `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md:19` — catalog row: "Vertical dive
    toward player (x locked at formation slot)".
  - `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md:711` — §7.3: "Dives are x-locked at
    the formation slot." (the preceding sentence already correctly records the
    dive-start snapshot).
  - `docs/Game Design Document.md:196` — §4.1 E2 Diver: "Dives straight down
    toward the player (x locked at its formation slot — a vertical trajectory)".
    Note: the source work item labelled this §4.2; the current GDD places E2 in
    **§4.1 Enemy Types** (§4.2 is Wave/Formation Structures).
- A repository-wide search confirms these are the only Diver dive trajectory
  references in `docs/`; no test asserts the stale wording, so no test updates
  are required.

## Desired change

Correct the three documentation locations so they describe the diagonal
parabolic dive toward the player position snapshotted at dive start, retain and
make consistent the snapshot-at-dive-start wording, and cross-reference the
superseding work item AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX. No code, test, or behavioural change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §1 enemy catalog row (E2 Diver) and
  §7.3 live aim tracking Diver bullet: replace x-locked wording with the diagonal
  bezier description and reference AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.1 E2 Diver behaviour bullet: state the
  diagonal dive toward the snapshotted player position.
- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — reference only (confirm `_startDive`/`_handleDive`
  behaviour and the `setAimTarget` snapshot doc comment); no code change expected.
- `src/entities/Diver.test.ts` — **comment-only** correction at lines 128-130
  (stale "x is locked at the dive-start slot" comment); no assertion or
  behavioural change. Producer-confirmed in-scope under AC4 (OPEN QUESTION 1).

## Related work

- **AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX — "Diver should rotate to face the player and dive towards
  them"** (completed, shipped v0.1.3) — the superseding change that made the dive
  diagonal toward the snapshotted player position and removed the x-lock; this
  item corrects the docs to match it.
- **AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB — "Fix Diver.ts: lock x during dive and smooth return to
  current formation slot"** (completed) — established the original x-lock that
  AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX superseded.
- **AH-0MTEI3HEX004070O — "Update documentation for Diver dive/return fix"**
  (completed) — prior documentation update around the dive/return fix; the
  x-locked wording this item corrects likely originates here.
- **AH-0MUAYB6KL005A09Q — "Divers do not kill the player"** (deleted) — the item
  this work was discovered from; it flagged the stale x-locked documentation as a
  risk.
- **AH-0MTEHZNY9008O98Y — "Write AC1: no horizontal movement during dive test"**
  (completed) — the vertical-drop-era test now superseded by the diagonal dive.
- **AH-0MUAYB957002EMYV — "Divers should not return"** (open) — adjacent Diver
  dive/return behaviour work that may touch the same docs sections (§7.6
  formation hold).
- **AH-0MTECNI8K008FSKH — "Implement: Core scene — enemy live aim tracking"**
  (completed) — records the snapshot seam decision referenced by §7.3.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — recurring doc drift:** the GDD and the implementation guide duplicate
  the Diver dive contract, so a future behaviour change can re-stale one without
  the other. Mitigation: update both in one change and cross-reference the
  superseding work item.
- **Risk — incomplete search:** wording variants (e.g. "straight down",
  "vertical") could exist beyond the three greps found. Mitigation: AC3's
  repository search covers `docs/` for the Diver dive; the initial search found
  only the three locations.
- **Risk — scope creep:** adjacent §7.6 / gym-parity documentation could be seen
  as in scope. Mitigation: constrain to the dive trajectory wording; record other
  drift as linked work items.
- **Assumption:** the implemented diagonal bezier and dive-start snapshot are the
  intended, correct contract (confirmed by the completed, audited
  AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX and the `Diver.ts` implementation).
- **Assumption:** no test **assertion** asserts the stale Diver doc wording, so
  this is a test-neutral change (verified by repository search). A stale
  **comment** does exist in `src/entities/Diver.test.ts:128-130`; the producer
  confirmed it is in scope as a comment-only edit (OPEN QUESTION 1).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No clarifying questions were required.** The seed context (the work item
  description with its three named locations and expected behaviour) plus a
  repository and worklog search sufficed to draft a complete, testable brief.
  No operator input was needed, so none was requested.
- **Research summary:** Read the three named locations
  (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1 catalog and §7.3,
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.1 E2 Diver) and confirmed each still states
  x-locked / vertical-only behaviour. Read `src/entities/Diver.ts`
  (`_startDive`, `_handleDive`, `_updateFacingRotation`, `setAimTarget`) and the
  completed audit of AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX, confirming the shipped behaviour is a
  diagonal quadratic-bezier dive toward the position snapshotted at dive start
  (x-lock removed). A `docs/` search found only those three stale references and
  no test asserting the stale wording. Noted that the source work item cited GDD
  §4.2 for E2, but E2 currently lives in §4.1 (recorded in Existing state).
- **Correction recorded (no answer required):** the GDD section reference is
  §4.1, not §4.2 as stated in the original work item description.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG** – Diver has no audio (completed)
- **AH-0MT94ULUU001NBW3** – Audit merge gate hard-codes npm run build; docs-only repos fail Phase 1 (completed)
- **AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5** – Game Design Document for AI_Hell (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: ac3, acceptance, actual, aim, alter (+52 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, aim, alter (+52 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, actual, aim, alter, arc (+51 more)


## Plan review (plan skill, 2026-09-27)

- **Plan decision: `plan_complete` via the auto-complete path.** Effort
  Extra Small / risk Low — below the decomposition threshold, so **no child
  work items were created**. The item is a single docs-only vertical slice
  (documentation edits + verification of the full test suite).
- **Fourth drift instance found (same topic — a stale code comment):**
  `src/entities/Diver.test.ts:128-130` carries the stale comment *"x is locked
  at the dive-start slot: the snapshot path and B diverge only in y, and (x+y)
  both match the snapshot arc."* The same test's assertions immediately below
  follow the diagonal quadratic bezier on both axes, so only the **comment** is
  stale (no assertion change is implied). AC4 ("any relevant code comments
  remain accurate") covers code comments; the producer confirmed via **OPEN
  QUESTION 1** that this comment is in scope as a **comment-only** edit, so AC4
  and Key Files now name it explicitly.
- **Verified accurate (no change needed):** `src/entities/Diver.ts:354-355`
  ("Aim direction: straight down", `baseAngle = 0`) describes the **bullet
  spread direction**, not the dive trajectory, and remains correct. No gym
  scene (`src/scenes/gym/**`) or shared core carries a dive-trajectory claim.
- **Verified:** the three named `docs/` locations are the only stale
  documentation claims, and no **assertion** asserts the stale wording — so
  AC5 stays a regression guard and no test-assertion edits are required.

## Appendix: Plan review questions (OPEN QUESTIONs)

- **OPEN QUESTION 1 — Scope of the stale test comment** (directed to: producer;

  - **Question:** Should the stale comment at `src/entities/Diver.test.ts:128-130`

  - **Options:** (a) correct it in this item as a comment-only edit under AC4;

  - **Recommended:** (a) — it is the same drift, it is a code comment (AC4), and

Implement the beat clock module (`src/utils/beat.ts`)

## Summary
Create a new pure, unit-testable beat clock module that derives a beat period from a configurable BPM (default 80 BPM → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes quantisation helpers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — Module at `src/utils/beat.ts` exposes `beatPeriodMs` (derived from configurable BPM, default 80), `nextTick(elapsedTime, interval)`, and `shotTimeFor(currentTime, interval)` helpers.
- [ ] **AC2** — All helpers are pure and deterministic given an input time — no `Date` or frame coupling.
- [ ] **AC3** — The beat anchor is configurable (defaults to 0/scene start) and advances with game time (pauses with the game).
- [ ] **AC4** — Unit tests cover: period from BPM, quantisation boundaries/edge cases, config override changing cadence.
- [ ] **AC5** — Tests assert that `nextTick(t, interval)` returns the smallest multiple of `interval` at/after `t`, and `shotTimeFor` snaps to the correct grid tick.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC1** — [ ] **AC1 — Pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock.** A new pure, unit-testable module (e.g. `src/utils/beat.ts`) derives the beat period from a **configurable** BPM (default **80 BPM** → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes a quantisation helper that maps an arbitrary elapsed time to the next beat/subdivision tick (`nextTick(t)`, `isOnBeat/fireTimeFor(interval, t)`, etc.). No `Date`/frame coupling; deterministic given an input time.

## Constraints
- No audio or visual beat indicators — silent internal scheduling only.
- Must work with Phasers delta-time model (ms-based).
- Default BPM: 80 (beat period: 750 ms). All per-weapon intervals are exact subdivisions.

## Key Files
- `src/utils/beat.ts` — **NEW** — pure beat clock module.
- `src/utils/beat.test.ts` — **NEW** — unit tests.

## Risks
- Minimal: the module is pure and self-contained. Edge cases: large dt values (frame drops), zero elapsed time.

# Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview

## Context

The runtime auto-sequencer (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X) is fully implemented but not wired into the game. There is no way for designers or testers to interact with it visually. This work item creates a gym scene that provides a hands-on interface for designing and previewing difficulty curves.

discovered-from:AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X

## Goal

Add a new **Dev Utilities** category/section to the gym index, and create a gym scene within it that provides:

1. **Curve editor** — an interactive way to define the target difficulty curve (array of scores, one per wave)
2. **Regenerate button** — when clicked, runs the sequencer against the current curve and displays the resulting waves
3. **Wave list** — shows each generated wave with its enemy composition, target difficulty, and the resulting wave
4. **Edit-to-clear behaviour** — if the curve is edited, the wave list is cleared and replaced with an instruction to click the regenerate button

## Scope

- Add a **Dev Utilities** column/section to the gym index (GymIndex.ts) — follows the same pattern as the existing ENEMIES and Bosses columns
- Create src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts (and its test file)
- The scene uses the existing sequencer() from difficultySequencer.ts
- Plain-DOM tuning panel overlay (same pattern as GymPlayer) for the curve editor
- Phaser canvas for the wave list display (Phaser text objects)

## Curve editor design

- Each wave in the curve is represented as a row with:
  - A numeric slider (0–100) for the target difficulty
  - A Remove button to delete that wave row
- An "Add Wave" button to append a new wave row at the end
- The "Regenerate" button runs the sequencer and populates the wave list below
- When the curve is edited (any slider moved, wave added/removed), the wave list is cleared and replaced with instruction text: "Edit made — click Regenerate to preview"

## Wave list display

- Each wave entry shows:
  - Wave number
  - Target difficulty
  - Enemy composition (enemy type, count)
  - Whether shooting is enabled
- Entries rendered as Phaser text objects, ordered top-to-bottom

## Non-goals

- Saving/loading curves (could be added later)
- Visual preview of enemy formations (text-only for now)
- Drag-to-reorder waves in the curve editor

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Gym index shows a "Dev Utilities" section** — a new column or section in the gym index listing gym scenes under the Dev Utilities category
2. **GymCurveSequencer scene is listed** under the Dev Utilities section and can be launched from the gym index
3. **Curve editor works** — user can add wave rows, remove wave rows, and adjust target difficulty via sliders (0–100)
4. **Regenerate button** — clicking it runs sequencer() with the current curve and candidate pool, populating the wave list
5. **Wave list is cleared on curve edit** — when the user edits the curve (any change), the wave list is replaced with instruction text to click regenerate
6. **Wave entries display correctly** — each shows wave number, target difficulty, enemy composition, and shooting status
7. **Back to index button** works (arrow-left INDEX)
8. **ESC returns to main menu** (consistent with other gym scenes)
9. **All tests pass** — the scene has unit tests verifying the curve editor and regenerate flow

## Revision — audit follow-up (2026-09-27)

Manual review rejected the first implementation with the following note:

> Rejected by manual review. Make the wave description a table, with column headings. Provide a help box in the bottom right summarizing each column.

Additional acceptance criteria:

10. **Wave preview is a table** — the wave preview renders a table with column headings (Wave, Target, Composition, Shooting) and one aligned row per wave.
11. **Column guide help box** — a help box anchored to the bottom-right of the canvas summarises each wave-table column.

## Revision — second audit follow-up (2026-09-27)

Manual review rejected the implementation again with the following note:

> Rejected by manual review. The UI works, but the generated levels are not good. Firstly, why do we have an actual and error value? Why don't we just create as close the target as possible? Secondly, the higher levels seem to just repeat the phaser with shooting.

Root cause confirmed by reproducing the sequencer output: `sequencer()` picked exactly one candidate group per wave and a single group's `enemyDifficulty` score saturates around 33 (e.g. `phaser×12`), so every target at or above ~40 produced the identical `phaser×12` wave — hence the large error values and the repetition.

Revised acceptance criteria:

12. **Wave generation reaches the target** — the preview table no longer shows redundant ACTUAL/ERROR columns; the table columns are WAVE / TARGET / COMPOSITION / SHOOTING. The sequencer composes a wave from one or more candidate groups so the wave's summed difficulty is within a small tolerance of the target across the full 0–100 slider range (previously capped at ~33).
13. **Higher waves are varied** — waves with different (especially higher) targets produce meaningfully different enemy compositions instead of every high wave repeating the same archetype (e.g. `phaser` with shooting).

## Key Files

- src/scenes/GymIndex.ts — add Dev Utilities section
- src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts — new scene
- src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.test.ts — tests for the scene
- src/core/difficultySequencer.ts — sequencer (extended to compose multi-group waves)
- src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts — existing scorer (read-only)
- src/core/enemyConfig.ts — existing enemy configs for candidate pool
- src/utils/gymNavigation.ts — shared back-to-index navigation
- src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts — gym scene auto-discovery (no changes needed, scene auto-appears)
data.title: Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview

# Goal

Fix the audit runner's parent-first flow so that child `partial` verdicts caused by unserviced in-main-slot items are treated as "not assessed" rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision, and add diagnostic clarity.

# Background

In `--child-in-main-slot` mode (default), child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking agent session. In non-interactive runs (e.g. downtime workers), these items are never serviced, leaving all child AC verdicts as `partial`.

Currently, `_build_issue_json` treats ALL `partial` verdicts as unacceptable, causing the parent to report "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met, because the child partials (from unserviced in-main-slot work) are counted as failures.

# Implementation Plan

## 1. Track in-main-slot partial verdicts

Add a `verdict_reason` field to child AC results when they are `partial` due to in-main-slot unserviced work. The `_phase1_review_child_acs` and `_deep_analyze_child` functions already set `verdict: "partial"` with evidence like `"pending (main-session review)"` in in-main-slot mode. We need to mark these explicitly with `verdict_reason: "unserviced-in-main-slot"`.

## 2. Handle partials in `_build_issue_json`

Modify `all_ac_acceptable` computation to skip child ACs whose `partial` verdict has `verdict_reason == "unserviced-in-main-slot"`. These should be treated as "not assessed" and NOT block the parent's readiness-to-close decision.

## 3. Add diagnostic output

In the audit summary/JSON output, surface a clear diagnostic that distinguishes:
- Children with `partial` verdicts from unserviced in-main-slot work → "not assessed"
- Children with genuine `partial` or `unmet` verdicts → "not-ready"

Add a `children_assessment` section to the `_build_issue_json` output listing `unserviced_in_main_slot` child IDs and `genuine_not_ready` child IDs.

# Acceptance Criteria
- AC2: Parent audit treats in-main-slot unserviced partials as "not assessed" (does NOT block ready-to-close)
- AC3: Audit output includes diagnostic distinguishing unserviced-in-main-slot partials from genuine failures

# Constraints
- Must not change behaviour of interactive runs (where agent CAN service in-main-slot items)
- Must be backward-compatible with persisted audit results

# Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase1_review_child_acs`, `_deep_analyze_child`, `_build_issue_json`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — existing in-main-slot tests
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — freshness tests (verify no regression)

# Goal

Verify the audit-runner fixes satisfy all parent acceptance criteria, add regression coverage, and confirm the full project test suite passes.

# Background

The parent work item (AH-0MUDYHPPC008F7PV) has 5 acceptance criteria. AC1 (fingerprint scoping) appears already implemented in `_compute_content_fingerprint` — this task must verify it, and close any remaining gap. AC2-AC3 are implemented by the sibling task. AC4 (no regression on interactive runs) and AC5 (full test suite passes) are verified here.

# Verification tasks

## 1. Verify AC1 — fingerprint scoping

Confirm `_compute_content_fingerprint` no longer includes the global git HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger. The existing tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` (`TestContentFreshnessGate`) should prove:
- `test_fingerprint_does_not_query_bare_head` — the whole-repo HEAD sha is not a fingerprint input
- `test_fingerprint_stable_for_unrelated_commit` — an unrelated commit leaves the fingerprint unchanged

If any gap remains (e.g. a bare `git rev-parse HEAD` call still leaks in), fix it.

## 2. Verify AC2/AC3 — in-main-slot partial handling and diagnostics

Add/verify tests that:
- A parent audit with children whose ACs are `partial` due to unserviced in-main-slot work reports "Ready to close: Yes" (when parent ACs are met)
- The audit JSON output includes the `children_assessment` diagnostic distinguishing unserviced-in-main-slot children from genuine-not-ready children
- A genuine `partial`/`unmet` child verdict still blocks the parent (regression guard)

## 3. Verify AC4 — no regression on interactive runs

# Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC3, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic unit + guard tests that pin the contract of the shared mineral kill-drop rule **before** it is implemented, so `PlayScene` and the gyms provably share one rule.

## Required coverage

- Small asteroid (`getSizeTier() === 'small'`) → exactly one mineral drop at the asteroid's death position.
- Large and medium asteroid → no direct drop (their small split children drop).
- Non-asteroid enemy that absorbed N minerals → re-drops between `mineralRedropFractionMin` and `mineralRedropFractionMax` of N, never more than N, at the death site, using a seeded RNG for determinism.
- Non-asteroid enemy with 0 absorbed minerals → no drops.
- Re-drop scatter stays within `MINERAL_REDROP_SCATTER_RADIUS` of the death site.

## Assumption

Shared helper module path: `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` exporting `resolveMineralKillDrops(scene, entity, rng): Mineral[]` (operator selected the shared-helper approach — see the parent item's Appendix).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume, and a repo-wide guard asserts it.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the shared rule and the guard; `npm test` for the new files passes.
- The unit tests are deterministic (seeded RNG, no reliance on `Math.random`) and cover every bullet under Required coverage.
- Tests fail before the implementation task lands and pass once it does.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` — new.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend guard.
- `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` — shared guard helper (extend if needed).
- `src/entities/__tests__/BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.

## Goal
As a developer, I want a documented, repeatable reproduction and root-cause analysis for the flaky `isTransitioning()` assertion, so the fix targets the real source and does not mask a production defect.

## Context
Parent: AH-0MUHA0MMP001DZ5C (Flaky PlayScene wave-transition test). Three recorded occurrences across different PlayScene transition tests (AC5 line 443, AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6 AC4 line 665, AH-0MU7JTF9W008B8HW AC4 line 594) all fail as `expect(scene.isTransitioning()).toBe(false -> true)` right after `killAllEnemies`. Leading hypotheses: **H1** — the live Phaser requestAnimationFrame loop advances the scene an unpredictable amount (during/after the fixed 150 ms `bootDelay`), draining the 1.5 s `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` timer before the assertion under parallel load; **H2** — `killAllEnemies` only checks `getAliveCount() === 0`, so a kill path that does not drive `_advanceAfterKill()`/`_startTransition()` leaves `isTransitioning()` false; **H3** — a genuine `WaveManager` `_enemiesAlive` register/unregister desync or transition-timer ordering defect.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause identified and documented: the flakiness source is demonstrated with evidence (a failing reproduction under parallel load plus the code path that produces the nondeterministic state), and recorded in a comment on the parent item.
- [ ] The analysis explicitly distinguishes test-harness nondeterminism from any production accounting/ordering bug in `PlayScene`/`WaveManager`.
- [ ] Each of H1, H2 and H3 is confirmed or eliminated with concrete evidence (code path, captured state dump, or reproduction log), not assumption.
- [ ] If the flake is not reproducible, a state-dump diagnostic and code-path analysis are recorded and the reason it cannot be reproduced is documented.


## Minimal Implementation
- Add a temporary diagnostic (log `transitionTimer`, `waveManager.enemiesAlive`, `getAliveCount()` around the failing assertion) or a state-dump hook.
- Run the focused `PlayScene.test.ts` transition tests repeatedly under parallel CPU load and capture a failure, or prove a bounded non-reproduction.
- Trace the code path from the final enemy kill to `_startTransition()` and from the real Phaser loop's `update()` -> `tick(dt)` to `_onTransitionComplete()`.

**Key Files:**
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts`

## Deliverables
- Root-cause comment on AH-0MUHA0MMP001DZ5C distinguishing H1/H2/H3.
- Reproduction command/script and captured evidence.

## Summary

Add the pure, engine-agnostic danger-detection helper that decides when the player is "in danger" (parent AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8). Per producer answers Q1 and Q5, danger is the **combined** count of hostile bodies and hostile bullets whose centre lies within `DANGER_RADIUS = 2 × SHIP_SIZE` (40 px) of the ship, and the player is in danger when that count is `>= DANGER_THREAT_THRESHOLD = 3`. This item is **test-first**: write the failing unit tests before implementing the helper.

## Why

Phase Shift becomes an automatic, reactive defensive tool; it needs a single, correct, unit-testable proximity judgement shared by every combat scene. Without it the auto-trigger has no input.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1.1 — `src/core/constants.ts` exports `DANGER_RADIUS` (= `2 * SHIP_SIZE`, i.e. 40 with `SHIP_SIZE = 20`) and `DANGER_THREAT_THRESHOLD` (= 3); both are used by the helper (no duplicated literals).
- [ ] AC1.2 — A pure helper (e.g. `countThreatsInRange(ship, bodies, bullets)` and `isInDanger(...)`) lives in `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts` with **no Phaser import**.
- [ ] AC1.3 — Counting is by **centre-to-centre** distance from the ship; a threat exactly on the radius boundary (distance == `DANGER_RADIUS`) counts as inside.
- [ ] AC1.4 — Boundary tests: exactly 3 combined threats → in danger; 2 → not in danger; a threat just inside the radius counts and one just outside does not.
- [ ] AC1.5 — Enemy bodies (asteroids, boss, boss minions and all enemy archetypes) and live enemy bullets count; player bullets and minerals do **not** count.
- [ ] AC1.6 — `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass; the new tests fail against the pre-change (absent-helper) implementation, demonstrating TDD.
- [ ] AC1.7 — JSDoc on the helper documents the 40 px / >= 3 rule and the producer decision (Q1/Q5).

- [ ] Traceability — parent AC1 (AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8): [ ] **AC1 — Danger detection is measurable and correct.** A pure, unit-testable helper counts hostile entities + hostile bullets within `2 × SHIP_SIZE` of the ship and reports "in danger" when the combined count is ≥ 3. Boundary cases are covered: exactly 3 threats triggers; 2 threats do not; threats just inside the radius count and just outside do not; asteroids, boss/minions and all enemy bullet types count; player bullets and minerals do not.


## Minimal Implementation

- Add the two constants to `src/core/constants.ts`.
- Create `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts` with a small, total, allocation-light API: `distanceSq`-based counting, accepting read-only `{x,y}` arrays so it is trivially testable and reusable from the scene.
- Add `src/powerups/dangerDetection.test.ts` covering AC1.3–AC1.5.

**Key Files:**
- `src/core/constants.ts`
- `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts`
- `src/powerups/dangerDetection.test.ts`

## Dependencies

None (foundational). Parent: AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8.

## Summary

Surface finite P6 auto-activation charges in the HUD (parent AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8), so a normally-collected Phase Shift shows how many uses remain while the permanent (hold-full) reward shows unlimited. Per producer answer Q3.

## Why

Charges are a new player-facing resource; without a HUD readout the deferred-use model is invisible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC6.1 — The HUD renders the current P6 auto-activation charge count from the shared `EffectsRegistry` aggregated model (no scene-local state).
- [ ] AC6.2 — One charge displays as `x1` and decrements live on trigger.
- [ ] AC6.3 — The permanent (hold-full) P6 displays as unlimited (e.g. `∞` / `PERM`) rather than a number.
- [ ] AC6.4 — Zero charges are not shown as an active effect (no misleading `x0`).
- [ ] AC6.5 — Unit tests cover charge formatting and the permanent/zero cases; existing HUD tests remain green.
- [ ] AC6.6 — `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the registry's `activeEffects()`/accessor surface with P6 charge state (consumed by C2) and render it in `src/ui/HUD.ts` alongside existing stack/timer values.
- Extend `src/ui/HUD` tests.
